data.title: Git: Introduce Rust and announce it will become mandatory in the build system
data.author: WhyNotHugo
data.article_summary: 该网站使用Anubis系统来防止AI公司大规模爬取数据，保护服务器稳定。Anubis采用类似Hashcash的工作量证明机制，对小规模用户影响微小，但能大幅增加大规模爬取的成本。系统目前是临时解决方案，未来会通过识别无头浏览器等技术改进验证方式。用户需启用现代JavaScript功能，禁用JShelter等插件才能正常访问。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[Git是否应该引入Rust作为可选依赖，并在未来成为强制依赖]

不同观点：
• **支持引入Rust**  
  - Rust可以作为可选依赖逐步引入，直到GCC支持Rust后再强制使用，这样可以平滑过渡  
  - Rust的内存安全性可以减少运行时错误，提升代码质量  

• **反对引入Rust**  
  - Git已经是成熟软件，不需要大量新代码，引入Rust增加了不必要的复杂性  
  - Rust学习曲线陡峭，增加了贡献者的门槛  
  - Rust的工具链复杂，混合语言开发降低了Git的可维护性和可扩展性  

• **中立或观望态度**  
  - 建议等待GCC对Rust的支持成熟后再决定是否强制依赖  
  - 需要更多信息了解Git未来的发展方向（如Git 3.0是否会破坏兼容性）  

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：Rust的复杂性和必要性是否值得在Git中引入  
- **用户视角**：普通用户关心这一变化是否能带来实际好处  
- **平台兼容性**：Rust在某些平台上可能难以支持  
- **开发文化**：是否忽视了跨平台编译的传统开发方式  
- **提案背景**：不清楚这是否是Git核心贡献者的共识，还是个别提案

45312696.article_content:
Making sure you're not a bot!
Loading...
You are seeing this because the administrator of this website has set up Anubis to protect the server against the scourge of AI companies aggressively scraping websites. This can and does cause downtime for the websites, which makes their resources inaccessible for everyone.
Anubis is a compromise. Anubis uses a Proof-of-Work scheme in the vein of Hashcash, a proposed proof-of-work scheme for reducing email spam. The idea is that at individual scales the additional load is ignorable, but at mass scraper levels it adds up and makes scraping much more expensive.
Ultimately, this is a placeholder solution so that more time can be spent on fingerprinting and identifying headless browsers (EG: via how they do font rendering) so that the challenge proof of work page doesn't need to be presented to users that are much more likely to be legitimate.
Please note that Anubis requires the use of modern JavaScript features that plugins like JShelter will disable. Please disable JShelter or other such plugins for this domain.

data.title: Overcoming barriers of hydrogen storage with a low-temperature hydrogen battery
data.author: rustoo
data.article_summary: 日本研究人员开发出一种可在90°C低温下运行的氢电池，突破了传统氢存储需要超低温或高温的限制。该电池使用新型固体电解质Ba0.5Ca0.35Na0.15H1.85，通过传导氢离子实现氢的可逆存储与释放。以氢化镁为阳极、氢气为阴极，电池实现了7.6wt.%的储氢容量，且性能稳定。这项技术为氢能源汽车和清洁能源系统提供了实用化的储氢方案。研究成果发表于《科学》期刊。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[氢能源存储技术的可行性及与其他能源技术的比较]

不同观点：
• [氢能源存储的实用性与挑战]
  - firesteelrain指出业余爱好者可以通过简单设备从水中生成氢气，且无需极端温度和压力存储，质疑论文中提到的极端存储条件的必要性。
  - enigma101认为电解过程中残留物积累会导致系统最终崩溃，质疑氢能源的长期可行性。
  - ilaksh询问是否需要持续维持90°C的温度，否则能量是否会流失。
  
• [氢能源与其他能源技术的比较]
  - bilsbie倾向于将氢与碳原子结合存储（甲烷），并询问这种方式的比较优势。
  - pfdietz认为电池技术已经足够满足地面交通工具的需求，氢能源的用途有限。
  - metalman批评氢能源基础设施的缺乏，并指出钠电池等替代技术已经实现规模化应用。

• [氢能源的未来发展潜力]
  - newyankee希望日本等氢能源投资国能在2030年突然推出突破性技术，补充现有电池技术的不足。
  - huijzer对氢能源技术的商业化前景持悲观态度，认为其难以实现大规模生产。
  - pkphilip对氢能源存储温度的降低表示赞赏，但对其效率提出疑问。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：氢能源的存储技术是否真的需要极端条件，以及其长期可行性和商业化前景。
• metalman的评论引发了关于氢能源基础设施和替代技术的激烈讨论，特别是与钠电池的比较。

45312447.article_content:
Overcoming the barriers of hydrogen storage with a low-temperature hydrogen battery
September 19, 2025
Scientists develop a solid electrolyte, utilizing which the battery stores and releases hydrogen at temperatures below 100 degrees Celsius
Press Releases
Research
Materials Science and Engineering
Chemical Science and Engineering
Mathematical and Computing Science
A hydrogen battery that operates at just 90 °C has been developed by researchers from Japan, overcoming the high-temperature and low-capacity limits of earlier methods. The device works by moving hydride ions through a solid electrolyte, allowing magnesium hydride, which acts as the anode, to repeatedly store and release hydrogen at full capacity. This battery offers a practical way to store hydrogen fuel, paving the way for hydrogen-powered vehicles and clean energy systems.
Solid Electrolyte for Low-Temperature Hydrogen Storage
High-Capacity, Reversible Hydrogen Storage Using H
‒
-Conducting Solid Electrolytes
Hirose <iet al
. (2025) |
Science
| 10.1126/science.adw1996
One of the most pressing challenges facing the use of hydrogen is its storage, which typically requires extremely low temperatures (−252.8 °C) and high pressures (350 to 700 bar). Instead of storing hydrogen as a gas or liquid, a more effective approach is to store it in solid materials such as magnesium hydride (MgH
2
), which has high theoretical storage capacity. This material can be integrated into a battery-like system where, instead of only moving electrons, hydrogen itself is stored and released during charging and discharging.
Until recently, this approach was limited by the need for high operating temperatures above 300 °C, poor reversibility of hydrogen absorption and desorption, and unwanted side reactions that reduced performance. In a significant development that may open the door to practical applications, researchers from Institute of Science Tokyo (Science Tokyo), Japan, have developed a hydrogen battery that can operate at much lower temperatures, around 90 °C. The study published in the journal
Science
on September 18, 2025, was conducted by a research team led by Research Scientist Dr. Takashi Hirose, Assistant Professor Naoki Matsui, and Institute Professor Ryoji Kanno at the Research Center for All-Solid-State Battery in Science Tokyo.
“We demonstrated the operation of an Mg–H
2
battery as a safe and efficient hydrogen energy storage device, achieving high capacity, low temperature, and reversible hydrogen gas absorption and release,” says Matsui.
The novelty of this battery lies in its solid electrolyte, Ba
0.5
Ca
0.35
Na
0.15
H
1.85
, which can transport hydrogen ions, specifically hydride ions (H
–
), efficiently. This material has an anti-α-AgI-type crystal structure, well known for its superionic conductivity. In this structure, barium, calcium, and sodium occupy body-centered positions, while H
–
move through face-sharing tetrahedral and octahedral sites, allowing them to migrate freely. Tests showed that the material has high ionic conductivity at room temperature (2.1 × 10
-5
S cm
-1
) and electrochemical stability, making the system effective for long-term hydrogen storage and release.
The battery design uses MgH
2
as the anode and hydrogen (H
2
) gas as the cathode. During charging, MgH
2
releases H
–
, which migrate through the Ba
0.5
Ca
0.35
Na
0.15
H
1.85
electrolyte to the H
2
electrode, where they are oxidized to release H
2
gas. During discharging, the reverse occurs: H
2
gas at the cathode is reduced to H
–
, which move through the electrolyte to the anode and react with Mg to form MgH
2
.
This process allows the cell to both store and release H
2
when needed, all at manageable temperatures below 100 °C. Using this cell, the researchers were able to reach the full theoretical storage capacity of MgH
2
, about 2,030 mAh g
-1
, equivalent to 7.6 wt.% H
2
, over repeated cycles.
Traditional solid-state hydrogen storage methods have faced major limitations. Heat-driven absorption and desorption required very high operating temperatures between 300 and 400 °C to release or capture hydrogen, which made the process energy-intensive and impractical for everyday use. An alternative approach using electrochemical storage with liquid electrolytes at lower temperatures suffered from poor hydrogen-ion transport, which meant that the materials could not achieve anywhere near their theoretical storage capacities. As a result, both approaches fell short of providing an efficient, reversible, and low-temperature solution for hydrogen storage.
“These properties of our hydrogen storage battery were previously unattainable through conventional thermal methods or liquid electrolytes, offering a foundation for efficient hydrogen storage systems suitable for use as energy carriers,” explains Hirose.
Such a battery could be key to a hydrogen-powered future, enabling hydrogen-powered vehicles and carbon-free industries.

Takashi Hirose

, Naoki M

data.title: High-performance read-through cache for object storage
data.author: pranay01
data.article_summary: Cachey是一个高性能的读取缓存系统，专为对象存储设计。它具有以下特点：1) 提供简单HTTP API；2) 采用内存+磁盘混合缓存架构；3) 支持S3兼容后端存储；4) 使用16MB固定页面大小；5) 能合并相同页面的并发请求；6) 支持冗余存储桶。核心API通过/fetch/{kind}/{object}端点获取数据，可配置Range范围和存储桶优先级。系统还提供/stats和/metrics监控端点，支持Docker部署，可通过命令行参数配置缓存大小、磁盘路径等。该项目采用MIT许可证开源。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[S2缓存技术的适用场景、优势和潜在问题]

不同观点：
• [技术扩展性]  
- rwmj提出可以通过NBD前端插件将不可变对象转化为Linux设备或qemu虚拟磁盘，增强实用性  
- mertleee呼吁将S2技术下沉为IoT边缘中间件，认为其边缘协议有巨大潜力  

• [生产环境适用性质疑]  
- onethumb指出该技术可能仅适合单可用区系统，缺乏对多AZ高可用生产环境的支持，并质疑跨区域缓存一致性和成本问题  
- denis_dolya认同其混合缓存设计的创新性，但指出大数据流和特定后端可能存在局限性  

• [实际应用场景探讨]  
- _1tan询问该技术相比直接S3读取的优势场景，特别关注Java应用的检索加速可能性  
- OutOfHere更倾向于应用内建缓存，认为外部缓存会增加键值失效的管理复杂度  

补充讨论：[争议焦点]  
主要争议集中在：1）技术是否适合分布式生产环境（跨AZ一致性vs单AZ优化） 2）外部缓存与内建缓存的价值权衡（管理复杂度vs性能收益）

Cachey
High-performance read-through cache for object storage.
Simple HTTP API
Hybrid memory + disk cache powered by
foyer
Designed for caching immutable blobs
Works with any S3-compatible backend, but has its own
/fetch
API requiring a precise
Range
Fixed page size (16 MiB) – maps requested byte range to page-aligned lookups
Coalesces concurrent requests for the same page
Makes hedged requests to manage tail latency of object storage
Can attempt redundant buckets for a given object
Motivating context
API
Fetching data
Request
HEAD|GET /fetch/{kind}/{object}
kind
+
object
form the cache key
kind
identifies the bucket set (up to 64 chars)
object
is the S3 object key
Header
Required
Description
Range
yes
Byte range in format
bytes={first}-{last}
C0-Bucket
no
Bucket(s) containing the object
C0-Config
no
Override S3 request config
C0-Bucket
behavior:
Multiple headers indicate bucket preference order
If omitted,
kind
is used as the singular bucket name
Client preference may be overridden based on internal latency/error stats
At most 2 buckets attempted per page miss
C0-Config
overrides:
Space-separated key-value pairs to override S3 request configuration per page miss.
ct=<ms>
Connect timeout (in case an existing connection could not be reused)
rt=<ms>
Read timeout (time-to-first-byte)
ot=<ms>
Operation timeout (across retries)
oat=<ms>
Operation attempt timeout
ma=<num>
Maximum attempts
ib=<ms>
Initial backoff duration
mb=<ms>
Maximum backoff duration
Example Request
GET
/fetch/prod-videos/movie-2024.mp4 HTTP/1.1
Range:
bytes=1048576-18874367
C0-Bucket:
us-west-videos
C0-Bucket:
us-east-videos-backup
C0-Config:
ct=1000 oat=1500 ma=5 ib=10 mb=100
Response
The service maps requests to 16 MiB page-aligned ranges and the response has standard HTTP semantics (
206 Partial Content
,
404 Not Found
etc.)
Header
Description
Content-Range
Actual byte range served
Content-Length
Number of bytes in response
Last-Modified
Timestamp from first page
Content-Type
Always
application/octet-stream
C0-Status
Status for first page
C0-Status
format:
{first}-{last}; {bucket}; {cached_at}
Byte range and which bucket was used
cached_at
is Unix timestamp with 0 implying a cache miss
Only first page status is sent as a header; status for subsequent pages follows the body as trailers
Example Response
HTTP/1.1 206 Partial Content
Content-Range:
bytes 1048576-18874367/52428800
Content-Length:
17825792
Content-Type:
application/octet-stream
C0-Status:
1048576-16777215; us-west-videos; 1704067200
<data>
C0-Status:
16777216-18874367; us-west-videos; 0
Monitoring
GET /stats
returns throughput stats as JSON for load balancing and health checking.
GET /metrics
returns a more comprehensive set of metrics in Prometheus text format.
Command line
Docker images
are available.
Usage: server [OPTIONS]
Options:
--memory <MEMORY>
Maximum memory to use for cache (e.g., "512MiB", "2GB", "1.5GiB") [default: 4GiB]
--disk-path <DISK_PATH>
Path to disk cache storage, which may be a directory or block device
--disk-kind <DISK_KIND>
Kind of disk cache, which may be a file system or block device [default: fs] [possible values: block, fs]
--disk-capacity <DISK_CAPACITY>
Maximum disk cache capacity (e.g., "100GiB") If not specified, up to 80% of the available space will be used
--hedge-quantile <HEDGE_QUANTILE>
Latency quantile for making hedged requests (0.0-1.0, use 0 to disable hedging) [default: 0.99]
--tls-self
Use a self-signed certificate for TLS
--tls-cert <TLS_CERT>
Path to the TLS certificate file (e.g., cert.pem) Must be used together with --tls-key
--tls-key <TLS_KEY>
Path to the private key file (e.g., key.pem) Must be used together with --tls-cert
--port <PORT>
Port to listen on [default: 443 if HTTPS configured, otherwise 80 for HTTP]

data.title: Calculator Forensics (2002)
data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary: 这篇文章列出了多种计算器型号对特定数学公式"arcsin(arccos(arctan(tan(cos(sin(9))))))"的计算结果，并按结果值排序。结果显示不同品牌和型号的计算器（如APF、Casio、Sharp、HP等）给出了从0.0到8.99998762105不等的数值，反映了不同芯片组和计算器设计的精度差异。测试数据包含计算器型号、芯片组及显示类型（VFD、LCD等）等信息，可作为评估计算器精度的参考依据。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[不同计算器在计算特定数学表达式时的结果差异及其原因]

不同观点：
• **支持从父页面开始讨论**  
  - [LeoPanthera]认为应从父页面开始，以获取完整背景信息，并提供了链接。

• **数学计算结果的差异**  
  - [avipars]通过Wolfram Alpha计算，给出了一个精确结果（0.424...），与某些计算器的结果不同。  
  - [OskarS]提到`math.h`在浮点和双精度下的计算结果接近9，但未完全匹配任何选项，指出超越函数的精度问题。  
  - [petters]指出数值计算困难，因为中间值接近余弦函数的局部最大值。

• **对计算器性能的评论**  
  - [tiahura]对HP-48的结果表示失望。  
  - [qiqitori]验证了Commodore SR-37的结果与SR-36一致（9.08210803）。  
  - [harshreality]希望看到更多现代计算器（如HP Prime、TI Nspire等）的测试结果。

• **幽默与哲学讨论**  
  - [kazinator]调侃“计算器是否犯下了数值分析的罪行”。  
  - [quirkot]提出哲学问题：如果AGI的芯片给出错误答案，它如何自知？

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：计算结果的正确性及其原因，尤其是超越函数的精度问题。  
- **历史背景**：[_trampeltier]提到曾向年轻人展示该网站，说明其教育意义。  
- **重复讨论**：[tomhow]指出此前已有多次相关讨论，并提供了历史链接。

不同观点：
• **支持Mojo的观点**  
  - Mojo结合了Rust的性能和安全优势，同时学习曲线更低，可能成为Rust和Go的竞争者。  
  - Mojo专注于系统软件，并可能通过移除异常等改进提升实用性（如[lordofgibbons]所述）。  
  - Mojo兼容Python生态且性能优异，能直接编译为可执行文件并优化GPU访问（如[rvz]所述）。  
  - 替代CUDA并提升LLVM的多线程支持可能带来开发效率的革命（如[GeekyBear]所述）。

• **对Mojo的质疑或中立观点**  
  - Mojo试图将Python改造成高性能并行系统可能并不合适，但目标用户是Python程序员，因此缺乏更好选择（如[timmg]所述）。  
  - 深度学习领域专用语言（DSL）的时机已过，Mojo可能仅是“虚荣项目”（如[lqstuart]所述）。  
  - 注册使用Mojo的门槛（如登录）可能影响用户体验（如[behnamoh]所述）。

• **其他相关讨论**  
  - 部分用户更关注Mojo作为编程语言本身而非ML功能（如[rubymamis]所述）。  
  - 技术替代方案：Julia用户提到已实现类似功能（如[Archit3ch]所述）。  
  - 争议点：Apple为何不竞争Nvidia（如[roansh]提问，但未展开）。

补充讨论：  
- **争议焦点**：Mojo是否真能解决Python在生产环境中的维护性问题，以及其“Python兼容性”是否足以吸引开发者迁移。  
- **潜在障碍**：“Yet another language”的推广难度（如[timmg]提及）和公司控制语言的风险（如[rvz]反驳的反对观点）。

data.title: 40k-Year-Old Symbols in Caves Worldwide May Be the Earliest Written Language
data.author: mdp2021
data.article_summary: 考古学家在世界各地洞穴中发现了距今4万年的符号，可能是最早的书面语言。研究表明，这些符号包括点、线、三角形等32种形式，跨越数万年保持惊人的一致性。古人类学家冯·佩辛格认为这代表人类早期抽象思维能力的发展，可能是现代信息交流网络的雏形。但学术界对此存在争议，有学者认为这些符号仅与动物形象相关。MIT语言学家则提出新理论，认为洞穴艺术可能是将声音转化为图像的早期语言表达形式。这些发现可能改写文字起源的历史，将书面语言的诞生时间大幅提前。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：冰河时代洞穴中的抽象符号是否为最早的书面语言或原始文字系统。

不同观点：
• **支持符号系统论**：认为这些符号（点、线、Y形等）可能是原始记事系统或月历，与动物生命周期相关，但并非真正的书写系统。论据包括符号的重复出现和跨文化分布，但缺乏语法或语言编码证据（如nelox和JoeDaDude的评论）。
• **反对语言关联论**：认为这些符号仅是装饰或独立认知产物，与语言无关。论据包括符号的普遍性（如儿童自发绘制）和缺乏语言学证据（如geor9e和BrenBarn的批评）。争议焦点在于符号是否具备传递复杂信息的能力。
• **批评研究方法**：指出现有研究存在过度解读（如ajross称插图为“垃圾科学”）或证据不足（如txru要求更严格的时空关联证据）。争议焦点包括符号跨地域/时间的关联性是否成立。
• **文化符号论**：提出符号可能用于非语言目的，如认知实验或艺术表达（如pkdpic和sharpshadow强调符号的认知或环境指示功能）。

补充讨论：
• 历史语言学的类比争议：如txru提及“阿尔泰语系”假说的失败，警示跨文化符号关联的论证风险。
• 媒体夸大问题：原始研究未声称发现“文字”，但标题引发误解（如JoeDaDude指出TED演讲仅称“图形沟通”）。
• 极端理论参考：如aa-jv提到的“Protong”全球语言假说，虽被主流否定，但引发对符号普遍性的思考。

40,000-Year-Old Symbols Found in Caves Worldwide May Be the Earliest Written Language
in
History
,
Language Lessons
|   	September 17th, 2025
42 Comments
We may take it for grant­ed that the ear­li­est writ­ing sys­tems devel­oped with the Sume­ri­ans around 3400 B.C.E. The archae­o­log­i­cal evi­dence so far sup­ports the the­o­ry. But it may also be pos­si­ble that the ear­li­est writ­ing sys­tems pre­date
5000-year-old cuneiform tablets
by sev­er­al thou­sand years. And what’s more, it may be pos­si­ble, sug­gests pale­oan­thro­pol­o­gist
Genevieve von Pet­zinger
, that those pre­his­toric forms of writ­ing, which include the ear­li­est known hash­tag marks, con­sist­ed of sym­bols near­ly as uni­ver­sal as emo­ji.
The study of sym­bols carved into cave walls all over the world—including pen­ni­forms (feath­er shapes), clav­i­forms (key shapes), and hand stencils—could even­tu­al­ly push us to “aban­don the pow­er­ful nar­ra­tive,” writes
Frank Jacobs at Big Think
, “of his­to­ry as total dark­ness until the Sume­ri­ans flip the switch.” Though the sym­bols may nev­er be tru­ly deci­pher­able, their pur­pos­es obscured by thou­sands of years of sep­a­ra­tion in time, they clear­ly show humans “undim­ming the light many mil­len­nia ear­li­er.”
While bur­row­ing deep under­ground to make cave paint­ings of ani­mals, ear­ly humans as far back as 40,000 years ago also devel­oped a sys­tem of signs that is remark­ably con­sis­tent across and between con­ti­nents. Von Pet­zinger spent years cat­a­logu­ing these sym­bols in Europe, vis­it­ing “52 caves,” reports
New Scientist’s Ali­son George
, “in France, Spain, Italy and Por­tu­gal. The sym­bols she found ranged from dots, lines, tri­an­gles, squares and zigza­gs to more com­plex forms like lad­der shapes, hand sten­cils, some­thing called a tec­ti­form that looks a bit like a post with a roof, and feath­er shapes called pen­ni­forms.”
She dis­cov­ered 32 signs found all over the con­ti­nent, carved and paint­ed over a very long peri­od of time. “For tens of thou­sands of years,” Jacobs points out, “our ances­tors seem to have been curi­ous­ly con­sis­tent with the sym­bols they used.” Von Pet­zinger sees this sys­tem as a car­ry­over from mod­ern humans’ migra­tion into Europe from Africa. “This does not look like the start-up phase of a brand-new inven­tion,” she writes in her book
The First Signs: Unlock­ing the mys­ter­ies of the world’s old­est sym­bols
.
In her TED Talk at the top, von Pet­zinger describes this ear­ly sys­tem of com­mu­ni­ca­tion through abstract signs as a pre­cur­sor to the “glob­al net­work of infor­ma­tion exchange” in the mod­ern world. “We’ve been build­ing on the men­tal achieve­ments of those who came before us for so long,” she says, “that it’s easy to for­get that cer­tain abil­i­ties haven’t already exist­ed,” long before the for­mal writ­ten records we rec­og­nize. These sym­bols trav­eled: they aren’t only found in caves, but also etched into deer teeth strung togeth­er in an ancient neck­lace.
Von Pet­zinger believes, writes George, that “the sim­ple shapes rep­re­sent a fun­da­men­tal shift in our ances­tors’ men­tal skills,” toward using abstract sym­bols to com­mu­ni­cate. Not every­one agrees with her. As the
Brad­shaw Foun­da­tion notes
, when it comes to the Euro­pean sym­bols, emi­nent pre­his­to­ri­an Jean Clottes argues “the signs in the caves are always (or near­ly always) asso­ci­at­ed with ani­mal fig­ures and thus can­not be said to be the first steps toward sym­bol­ism.”
Of course, it’s also pos­si­ble that both the signs and the ani­mals were meant to con­vey ideas just as a writ­ten lan­guage does. So argues
MIT lin­guist Cora Lesure
and her co-authors in a paper pub­lished in
Fron­tiers in Psy­chol­o­gy
last year. Cave art might show ear­ly humans “con­vert­ing acoustic sounds into draw­ings,”
notes Sarah Gibbens at Nation­al Geo­graph­ic
. Lesure says her research “sug­gests that the cog­ni­tive mech­a­nisms nec­es­sary for the devel­op­ment of cave and rock art are like­ly to be anal­o­gous to those employed in the expres­sion of the sym­bol­ic think­ing required for lan­guage.”
In oth­er words, under her the­o­ry, “cave and rock [art] would rep­re­sent a modal­i­ty of lin­guis­tic expres­sion.” And the sym­bols sur­round­ing that art might rep­re­sent an elab­o­ra­tion on the theme. The very first sys­tem of writ­ing, shared by ear­ly humans all over the world for tens of thou­sands of years.
Note: An ear­li­er ver­sion of this post appeared on our site in 2019.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[Ellen Langer的研究是否可信及其心理学研究的可重复性]

不同观点：
• **质疑研究可信性**  
  - patel011393指出其他学者对Langer的研究提出了质疑，认为她的研究结果未被独立复现，且存在诸多问题（如PubPeer上的详细批评）。  
  - cadamsdotcom提到心理学领域的“可重复性危机”，质疑该研究是否可重复。  
  - FarMcKon认为研究结果“好得不真实”，并强调非凡的主张需要非凡的证据，而这项研究缺乏此类证据。  

• **支持或部分认可心理状态对行为的影响**  
  - m3047提出“功能性叠加”的概念，认为心理或身体受伤后行为改变可能持续，间接支持心理状态对行为的影响。  
  - sandspar通过个人观察指出，父亲回忆年轻时的故事时会短暂显得更有活力，认为这种心理影响是真实的。  

• **中立或生活化解读**  
  - ookblah以自身健身经历为例，认为年龄增长会导致行为调整，但并非完全放弃努力，暗示心理与行为的互动是渐进的。  
  - SamBam质疑环境重现是否能真正逆转衰老迹象，认为情绪态度可能起关键作用。  

补充讨论：  
- **争议焦点**：研究的科学性与可重复性（如patel011393与FarMcKon的批评 vs. sandspar的观察支持）。  
- **其他讨论点**：  
  - opminion和nickdothutton将研究类比为怀旧体验或科幻情节，偏向轻松解读。  
  - sebmellen批评文章写作质量，怀疑是AI生成，但与核心讨论关联较弱。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个名为iNapGPU的纯TTL门电路构建的文本模式显卡项目。作者受到Ben Eater"世界上最差的显卡"启发，设计了这个分辨率800x600@60Hz（实际可用400x300）的单色显卡。该项目使用了21个集成电路，包括计数器、TTL门电路、EPROM和SRAM，支持最多4种字符集，可通过Arduino或Z80等设备控制。文章详细说明了设计思路、电路实现中的优化与错误（如同步计时器的设计），并提供了测试代码和字符集转换工具。作者坦言这个设计存在缺陷，建议使用FPGA实现会更可靠。

主要讨论点：[DIY文本模式显示设备的性能优化与设计特点]

不同观点：
• **性能优化派**  
  - [duskwuff]和[dmitrygr]强调技术改进：建议使用更快的逻辑系列（如74LS、74HC）和添加去耦电容以减少干扰和提升性能。  
  - 争议焦点：当前设计的稳定性和噪声问题是否因缺少去耦电容或低速逻辑导致。

• **怀旧与审美派**  
  - [fancyfredbot]和[em3rgent0rdr]认为小故障（如显示毛刺）增添了设备的独特魅力，无需追求完美。  
  - [M4R5H4LL]怀念早期无显卡时代的速度，希望现代系统能支持纯文本模式的高分辨率显示。

• **应用场景派**  
  - [anthk]提到适配经典游戏（如Nethack）的可能性，并讨论字体与屏幕尺寸的兼容性。  
  - [Shadowmist]赞赏对特殊字符集（如标准银河字母）的支持。

补充讨论：
- 历史情怀：[pjmlp]将项目比作Elektor杂志的经典DIY项目，引发对早期电子制作的共鸣。  
- 安全性质疑：[privatelypublic]幽默提问芯片如何防止“魔法烟雾”（即烧毁）释放，暗示对电路保护的关注。

iNapGPU 🖥
Text-mode graphics card, using only TTL gates.
Specs
VGA resolution 800x600@60Hz (accessible 400x300), mono
50x18 characters
up to 255 chars in charset, up to 4 charsets using 1Mbit EPROM
created using 2 counters, some TTL gates and EPROM with SRAM
parallel interface; works with arduino or Z80
terrible idea anyway, use fpga instead
total IC count: 21
supports latin alphabet with polish letters, and Standard Galactic Alphabet
Inspired by Ben Eater's "
World's worst video card
", I built myself something more.. worse? His video card was rather a digital frame, than a working video card. I fixed this - and I optimized the timer circuitry.
(anyway, i have to tell you that my english is not best, but i try)
I haven't built a computer yet, so the card is tested with Arduino Mega, as it have many pins and it's quite cheap. So, as long as you have 21 free pins on your microcontroller (or you have hooked some shift registers), you can connect the GPU card to almost anything - Arduino, ESP, STM etc. The test code for Mega is attached in this repository.
Here is how the card looks:
I know it's terrible, and soldering many, MANY connections with .12mm wire is terrible too, but it's how I done it. When I was creating the schematic, I didn't know that it will work - this is why I soldered it on protoboard. I suggest you to
do it on fpga 'cause everyone's life will be easier then
create a normal PCB, DIY or bought.
So - I'll skip the most obvious parts, and focus on the HSYNC timer.
The pixel clock is 20MHz - two times more than Ben's card. Instead of using 3 4bit counters, I used one, 12bit counter. The thing is, it's rated for 12MHz max. at 15V! This is why I DON'T GUARANTEE this will work for you; you should use those 4bit counters. (tip: for me only SMD versions of CD4040 worked) Next, the numbers from counter are going to NAND gates. There are two things with it - I'm comparing only "ones"of numbers, but Ben is comparing the entire number. The thing is, when I'm not comparing "zeros", the number will be "shown" multiple times, what luckily won't affect us. Since the RS flip-flop is activated once, activating it more times won't do anything. Same for resetting it. The signal from last pixel (528) is connected via NOT gate, as reset and clock are high active signals.
With the vertical timer the thing is same: normal CD4040 counter, with NAND gates and two RS flip-flops. And at this stage, I did a small mistake, just as Ben did: the timers are counting from 0. Thus, when the total amount of pixels in a row WILL be 528px, the first pixel is 0, and the last is 527. At least let's say it's not that important, as everything is working just fine. Another thing is, that the timer IS running at 37.(87)kHz, and physically we could achieve resolution 400x600 - but this is really bad idea. This is why the first bit of the counter is not used.
The heart of my GPU is in the last sheet. I've successfully connected RAM and ROM to timers, that generate actual image. I used M27C1001 with read time up to 100ns, and as far as I checked - version 45ns doesn't really change anything. The IC is UV EPROM with capacity of 1Mbit. Sadly, this decreases to "only" 128kbit, as I'm using the memory as 1bit memory. At least, it was enough for 4 charsets with 255 chars each.
The first 8 bits of address is a character from SRAM. The next four bits are rows, next three bits are columns, and last two bits are for chosing the codepage.
Also, you can select the actual color of the font.
As being said, the first 8 bits are connected to the SRAM. I used 2kB HM6116 IC, as I don't need more (there's only 900 chars to store). The tricky thing is connecting the entire card with the environment. I used tri-state logic buffers, 74LS245 and 74LS244 as most optimal choice. They're separating timers from the SRAM while writing, and separating data and address bus while timers are reading from SRAM. Also, I did there a small mistake, and connected '245 between SRAM and EPROM. The best solution here should be a latch, as it will store actual character for a moment, not clear the entire bus. This should work better than '245, but I don't have '373 at this moment.
And this is it! An actual video card from TTL gates, as I said. I'm giving to you tools to convert an image into a charset, and code I used for testing with Arduino.  On
this repository
is also code for my DIY eprom programmer. I hope you won't do this,

data.title: XAI's Colossus 2 – First Gigawatt Datacenter in the World
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: xAI正在建设全球首个吉瓦级数据中心Colossus 2，计划在2025年第三季度超越Meta和Anthropic的计算规模。该项目从2025年3月启动，仅用6个月就完成200MW冷却系统建设，速度远超同行。文章还透露xAI采用独特的强化学习方法，可能超越OpenAI等竞争对手。同时探讨了xAI的资金来源问题，包括中东投资和特斯拉关联等。报告分为两部分：前部分聚焦Colossus 2的技术突破，后部分分析Grok模型和xAI的长期发展潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于碳排放背后的动机和经济利益分配的争议。

不同观点：
• **批评资本主义体系**  
  认为当前的碳排放主要是为了满足少数富人的利益，特别是通过技术竞争（如“2%更好的模型”）来积累财富，而忽视了环境代价。核心论据是“老富人”为了微小的竞争优势不惜加剧气候危机。

• **隐含的贫富差距议题**  
  通过“old rich guys”与普通人的对比，暗示资源分配不公——环境成本由大众承担，而利益集中在精英阶层。争议焦点在于经济增长模式是否以牺牲公共利益为代价。

补充讨论：  
• 未直接提及但可延伸的争议：技术进步的合理性（“2%改进”是否值得） vs. 气候危机的紧迫性。  
• 评论带有情绪化措辞（如“dumping carbon as hard as we can”），可能引发对立场极端性的讨论。

Does xAI have a shot at becoming a frontier lab?
Much has been written about xAI’s Colossus 1. The Memphis build belongs in the history books: the largest AI training cluster, erected from scratch in 122 days. With roughly 200,000 H100/H200s and ~30,000 GB200 NVL72, it remains, today, the largest fully operational, single-coherent cluster (setting apart Google,
master of multi-datacenter-training
).
However, Colossus 1’s ~300 MW looks modest next to the Gigawatt-scale clusters under construction by
OpenAI
,
Meta
and
Anthropic
. Their hyperscaler partners are happy to leverage their balance sheet and win the market by throwing dollars at it.
Was xAI’s prowess a one-time wonder? Today we will publicize some data from our
industry leading datacenter model over the last year
that is accessible to clients. This is the our same proprietary data that called the Oracle deals many months ahead of the announcement.
Source:
SemiAnalysis Datacenter Industry Model
– note: there is a lag between Datacenter operational and GPUs operational – Google and exact figures available in model
Short answer: no
. xAI is still squarely in the frontier-AI race and is positioned to leapfrog most rivals again on compute. By our estimates, its total datacenter capacity for a single training cluster will surpass Meta Superintelligence and Anthropic by Q3 2025. The datacenter capacity will be ready for the GPUs to be moved in to create the largest single datacenter in the world, yet again. xAI has to raise the capital for those GPUs, but they have the allocations from Nvidia to have it fully training large scale models early next year.
Elon came up with
a new genius trick
to beat rivals at time-to-market. Colossus 2 will be an even more impressive achievement than xAI’s first cluster. Let’s dig in.
The first half of this report will dig into the Colossus 2 prowess. The second half will discuss Grok models, our mid-to-long term thoughts on xAI, and the
unique RL method
xAI is using that may lead them to leapfrog OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.

th

nd
, 2025, we count 119 air-cooled chillers on site, i.e.
roughly 200MW of cooling capacity
. That’s enough to power roughly 110k GB200 NVL72. And
an Elon tweet
shows some racks were already installed in July.
xAI built in six months what
took 15 months for Oracle, Crusoe and OpenAI!

data.title: Nvidia wants 10Gbps HBM4 to blunt AMD's MI450, report claims
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: NVIDIA要求内存供应商突破JEDEC标准，计划在2026年Vera Rubin平台上使用10Gb/s/pin的HBM4内存，以提升GPU带宽。相比JEDEC标准的8Gb/s/pin，10Gb/s版本可使单栈带宽达到2.56TB/s。但更高速度带来功耗、散热和良率挑战，NVIDIA可能根据不同型号采用分级配置。SK海力士已完成HBM4开发，三星采用4nm工艺追赶，AMD的MI450也计划采用HBM4竞争。NVIDIA此举旨在保持AI推理性能优势，但也面临供应链和功耗压力。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

45324865.article_content:
(Image credit: Nvidia)
Nvidia is pressing its memory vendors to push beyond JEDEC’s official HBM4 baseline. According to
TrendForce
, the company has requested 10Gb/s-per-pin stacks for its 2026 Vera Rubin platform, a move designed to raise per-GPU bandwidth ahead of AMD’s next-generation MI450 Helios systems.
At 8Gb/s per pin — the rate JEDEC specifies for HBM4 — a single stack delivers just under 2 TB/s across the new 2,048-bit interface. Raising that to 10Gb/s bumps the total to 2.56 TB/s per stack. With six stacks, a single GPU clears 15 TB/s of raw bandwidth.
Rubin CPX
, Nvidia's compute-optimized config built to handle the most demanding inference workloads, is advertised with 1.7 petabytes per second across a full NVL144 rack. The higher the pin speed, the less margin Nvidia needs elsewhere to hit those numbers.
But driving 10Gb/s HBM4 isn’t a given. Faster I/O brings higher power, tighter timing, and more strain on the base die. TrendForce notes that Nvidia may segment Rubin SKUs by HBM tier if costs or thermals spike. That means 10Gb/s parts for Rubin CPX and lower-speed stacks for the standard Rubin configuration. The fallback is already in view: staggered supplier qualification and extended validation windows to stretch yield.
You may like
SK hynix confirms 3GB GDDR7 memory modules are in the works
Nvidia shares Blackwell Ultra's secrets — NVFP4 boost detailed and PCIe 6.0 support
Kioxia’s new 5TB, 64 GB/s flash module puts NAND toward the memory bus for AI GPUs
SK hynix remains Nvidia’s dominant HBM supplier and says it has
completed HBM4 development
and is ready for mass production. The company has referenced “over 10Gb/s” capability but hasn’t published die specs, power targets, or process details.
Samsung, by contrast, is more aggressive on node migration. Its HBM4 base die is moving to 4nm FinFET, a logic-class node intended to support higher clock speeds and lower switching power. That could give Samsung an edge at the high end, even if SK hynix ships more volume. Micron has confirmed sampling of HBM4 with a 2,048-bit interface and bandwidth exceeding 2 TB/s, but hasn’t said whether 10Gb/s is in scope.
AMD’s MI450 is still on the horizon
, but the memory spec is already known. Helios racks are expected to support up to 432GB of HBM4 per GPU, giving AMD a route to match or exceed Nvidia on raw capacity. With CDNA 4, it also gains architectural upgrades that aim squarely at Rubin’s inference advantage.
Nvidia clearly wants to make memory faster. But the more it leans on 10Gb/s HBM4, the more exposed it becomes to supplier variation, yield risks, and rack-level power constraints at a time when the margin for error is shrinking.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[超声波刀具的创新性、实用性与市场定位]

不同观点：
• **支持创新与市场潜力**  
  - 认为超声波刀具是创新产品，具有独特优势（如更锋利的切割效果、减少维护需求）。  
  - 强调创始人Scott的专注与专业性，信任其产品开发能力（如定制机器人测试切割效率）。  
  - 目标用户包括科技爱好者、特殊需求人群（如手部残疾者），或追求便利的高端用户。  
  - 例：HeyImAlex提到愿意用单一低维护刀具替代传统高端刀具。  

• **质疑实用性与性价比**  
  - 认为传统刀具（如日本刀或Victorinox）已足够好用，且成本更低、无需充电。  
  - 担忧电子垃圾问题（电池寿命、未来废弃处理）。  
  - 视频展示缺乏真实厨房场景测试（如快速切洋葱、甜椒），可能夸大实用性。  
  - 例：whyenot指出传统刀具“5年后不会变成电子垃圾”。  

• **争议营销策略与定位**  
  - 部分用户反感广告风格（如直接销售式宣传），认为目标受众不明确。  
  - 另一些人被创始人故事吸引，认为“情感营销”有效（如thomascountz的评论）。  
  - 争议焦点：产品是否过度包装，或确实填补了市场空白。  

补充讨论：  
- **技术细节争议**：是否存在健康风险（如oakwhiz问及病原体雾化）？其他品牌是否已推出类似产品（idorosen提及369sonic）？  
- **小众需求**：多数人认为适合特定场景（如火锅切片），但非日常必需品。  
- **幽默与科幻联想**：用户调侃为“振动光剑”（jmarchello），反映对科技感的兴趣。

data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[微生物水泥超级电容器的可行性与潜在影响]

不同观点：
• **技术可行性**
  - [calibas]：质疑水泥强度是否会因微生物而减弱，但研究显示细菌最终增强了水泥的强度，初期孔隙增加但后期结构更稳定。
  - [seemaze]：关注现代混凝土中钢筋的氧化问题，提出微生物是否会影响钢筋氧化（混凝土主要失效模式）的疑问。
  - [brotchie]：比较能量密度，指出微生物水泥的能量密度远低于锂离子电池，质疑其实际应用价值。

• **潜在应用与影响**
  - [Nevermark]：通过科幻场景描述，提出水泥可能成为“活体”能源设备，颠覆传统认知，并暗示其可能用于对抗“系统”。
  - [lexicality]：对“湿件未来”（生物技术与材料结合）表示兴奋，认为这是科幻恐怖题材的延伸。
  - [bix6]：认可其作为概念验证的潜力，期待进一步开发。

• **幽默与隐喻**
  - [johnohara]：用“paving”双关调侃学术论文的表述方式，并邀请同行评审加入“学术双关语”讨论。
  - [thesebas]：引用动画梗，讽刺技术可能隐含的剥削性（“这是变相奴役”）。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：[VladVladikoff]对能量（Wh/kg）与功率（kW/kg）的区别提出疑问，涉及技术参数的理解分歧。
- **讨论关系**：[calibas]的强度分析回应了[Nevermark]中“活体水泥”的设想，而[brotchie]的能量密度质疑与技术乐观派（如[bix6]）形成对比。

data.title: PYREX vs. pyrex: What's the difference?
data.author: lisper
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[Pyrex玻璃制品材质差异及其市场策略]

不同观点：
• **材质差异与地域关系**  
  - 英国用户KaiserPro指出英国PYREX为硼硅酸盐玻璃，而美国用户抱怨其质量差，暗示美国产品可能使用钠钙玻璃。  
  - jzelinskie补充说明，欧洲产（如法国）PYREX为硼硅酸盐，而美国市场难以购得，需通过“矿物油测试”或标识（如“Made in France”）区分。  
  - dtrav总结三种类型：实验室用大写PYREX（硼硅酸盐）、美国小写pyrex（钠钙玻璃）、法国产Pyrex（硼硅酸盐）。

• **安全性与使用建议**  
  - bob1029认为材质差异对实际使用影响有限，关键在操作规范（如预热烤箱），并指出硼硅酸盐玻璃破碎时更危险。  
  - Mayzie提到爆炸案例，但强调大写/小写标识并非可靠判断依据。  
  - wyclif询问安全性和实用性，提及IKEA的“MIXTUR”系列可能更接近传统Pyrex。

• **市场策略与商标争议**  
  - pbhjpbhj批评Pyrex通过商标混淆（如PYREX/pyrex）进行市场细分，属于“诱饵调包”行为，主张公开供应链信息以保护消费者。  
  - ycombinatrix对康宁公司保留品牌但降低质量表示惊讶。  
  - giantg2强调“Pyrex”已是营销术语，需通过其他方式确认材质。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：是否应因商标滥用（同一品牌不同材质）撤销Pyrex的商标权（pbhjpbhj提出法律依据）。  
- **替代方案**：用户推荐其他品牌（如OXO、IKEA MIXTUR）或二手市场（owenthejumper建议Goodwill）。  
- **文化差异**：德国用户weinzierl提到硼硅酸盐玻璃的本地名称“Jenaer Glass”。  
- **测试方法**：矿物油测试（jzelinskie）和标识检查（zabzonk）被提及，但可靠性存疑。

data.article_summary: 英国、加拿大和澳大利亚于2025年9月21日正式承认巴勒斯坦国，成为首批采取这一举措的G7国家。英国首相斯塔默表示此举旨在推动"两国方案"和平进程，强调并非对哈马斯的奖励，同时宣布将在数周内对哈马斯相关人员进行制裁。以色列外交部谴责该决定是"对哈马斯的奖赏"。加拿大总理卡尼率先宣布承认决定，法国等其他西方国家预计将在联合国大会上跟进。保守党领袖巴德诺赫批评这一决定"绝对灾难性"，认为无条件承认变相奖励了恐怖主义。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[巴以冲突的解决路径、国际社会对巴勒斯坦的承认、巴勒斯坦人的代表性与责任]

不同观点：
• **长期解决路径分歧**  
  - ViewTrick1002提出三种可能的解决路径：南非/津巴布韦式的统一（导致原管理阶层流亡）、两国方案（逐步接受彼此）、或当前对巴勒斯坦人的种族灭绝（导致以色列孤立）。认为以色列政府实际选择第三种，但两国方案才是合理选择。  
  - FridayoLeary强调巴勒斯坦文化需要根本转变，并批评国际社会将巴勒斯坦人与哈马斯等组织绑定，同时指出巴勒斯坦人对暴力的支持（如哈马斯的高支持率）是问题核心。

• **国际承认的效用争议**  
  - uncircle质疑承认巴勒斯坦国的实际意义，认为这只是政治作秀（如英国工党为拉拢选民），无助于改善巴勒斯坦人处境。  
  - Aeolun反驳称，反对承认的论调忽视了承认本身的政治象征价值，与停止战争苦难并无直接矛盾。  
  - Simulacra指出“承认”更准确的表述应是“承认巴勒斯坦国的潜力”，暗示当前并非完全国家地位。

• **巴勒斯坦人的责任与权利**  
  - FridayoLeary批评国际社会双重标准：一方面剥夺巴勒斯坦人非土地相关的权利（如永久难民身份），另一方面忽视其自身对暴力的责任（如支持恐怖分子领导）。  
  - mikaTheThird延伸至中东其他土著民族（如亚述人）的被压迫问题，认为阿拉伯人等殖民者也需被问责。

• **争议焦点**  
  - 巴勒斯坦人的代表性问题：是否被错误关联到哈马斯等组织（FridayoLeary vs. 默认媒体叙事）。  
  - 国际承认的实质作用：政治象征还是无效姿态（uncircle vs. Aeolun）。  
  - 以色列行动的正当性：自卫还是种族灭绝（ViewTrick1002的第三种路径指控）。

补充讨论：  
- ethniccleanse提到批评对巴勒斯坦的“种族清洗”会被审查（如帖子被标记），反映讨论环境的敏感性。  
- Fizzadar呼吁恢复被标记的帖子，涉及平台对争议内容的管控。

The
UK
,
Australia
and
Canada
have all formally recognised Palestinian statehood
in a diplomatically significant – but highly symbolic – move that puts three major
US
allies at odds with the Trump administration.
The
British prime minister, Keir Starmer
, said the historic move was needed to “revive the hope of peace and a two-state solution” and stressed that it was not a reward for Hamas’ terrorism.
Starmer said his government will sanction Hamas figures in the coming weeks. He also urged Israel to lift restrictions at Gaza’s border to allow for a surge in humanitarian aid, and said the “death and destruction” in Gaza “must end”.
Israel’s foreign ministry said “recognition is nothing but a reward for jihadist Hamas”.
Canada technically became the first G7 nation to recognise a Palestinian state, making the announcement on social media shortly before Australia and the UK. “Canada recognises the state of Palestine and offers our partnership in building the promise of a peaceful future for both the state of Palestine and the state of Israel,” the Canadian prime minister, Mark Carney, wrote.
Other countries, including
France
, are expected to follow suit this week at the UN general assembly in New York.
Thanks for joining us. We are closing this blog now. You can find all our
latest coverage of UK politics here
.

data.title: Help us raise $200k to free JavaScript from Oracle
data.author: kaladin-jasnah
data.article_summary: Deno组织发起了一项募捐活动，旨在筹集20万美元，用于向美国专利商标局提交请愿，要求取消Oracle对"JavaScript"商标的所有权。Deno认为该名称已成为通用术语，不应被任何公司独占。目前案件已进入关键证据收集阶段，需要资金用于专业调查、专家证词和法律文件等。Oracle在2025年8月首次回应，否认"JavaScript"是通用术语。若请愿失败，Oracle将永久拥有该商标权。此次案件不仅关乎JavaScript，还涉及商标法是否真正保护公众利益。剩余资金将捐赠给OpenJS基金会。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Deno发起众筹以挑战Oracle对"JavaScript"商标权的行动是否合理，以及JavaScript名称的未来。

不同观点：
• 支持Deno的行动：
  - Illniyar认为Deno是在提供公共服务，即使有VC支持，向公众募资也是合理的。
  - scandox表示愿意为对抗Oracle捐款，即使平时很少这样做。
  - gtoast暗示有更富有的公司应该支持这一行动。

• 质疑Deno的行动：
  - SignalM认为Deno资金不足，无法与Oracle的法律团队抗衡，200k美元只是浪费。
  - hu3警告如果Deno准备不足，可能会在法庭上为Oracle创造不利先例。
  - maccard质疑VC支持的Deno为何需要众筹，暗示其动机不纯。

• 对JavaScript名称的争议：
  - siva7和thw_9a83c认为JavaScript名称不佳，建议改名如WebScript或JS。
  - billpg建议完全放弃"JavaScript"名称，仅使用"JS"。
  - throwingrocks和baalimago提到ECMAScript和TypeScript作为替代方案。

补充讨论：
• morpheuskafka指出Oracle在全球多国拥有商标，仅美国取消商标影响有限。
• ozgung提供历史背景，说明JavaScript名称和商标的由来。
• knotbin提到Deno创始人Ryan Dahl承认此举有营销目的，但否认是恶意行为。

45297066.article_content:
Help Us Raise $200k to Free JavaScript from Oracle
September 18, 2025
Ryan Dahl
#FreeJavaScript
After more than
27,000 people signed our open letter to Oracle
about the “JavaScript” trademark, we filed a formal
Cancellation Petition
with the US Patent and Trademark Office. Ten months in, we’re finally reaching
the crucial
discovery phase
.
Deno initiated this petition since we have legal standing as a JavaScript
runtime, but it’s really on behalf of all developers. If we win, “JavaScript”
becomes public domain – free for all developers, conferences, book authors, and
companies to use without fear of trademark threats.
We’re asking for your support through our
GoFundMe campaign
so we can put forward the strongest case possible.
Why $200k?
Because federal litigation is expensive. Discovery is the most
resource-intensive stage of litigation, where evidence is collected and
arguments are built.
We don’t want to cut corners – we want to make the best case possible by
funding:
Professional public surveys
that carry legal weight in front of the USPTO,
proving that “JavaScript” is universally recognized as the name of a language,
not Oracle’s brand.
Expert witnesses
from academia and industry to testify on JavaScript’s
history, usage, and meaning.
Depositions and records
from standards bodies, browser vendors, and
industry leaders showing Oracle has no role in the language’s development.
Legal filings and responses
to counter Oracle’s claims at every step.
If there are leftover funds, we’ll donate them to the
OpenJS
to continue defending civil
liberties in the digital space. None of the funds will go to Deno.
Oracle officially denies “JavaScript” is generic
On August 6th, 2025, Oracle for the first time addressed the validity of the
trademark.
Their response
to our
petition
denies that “JavaScript” is a generic term.
If you’re a web developer, it’s self-evident that Oracle has nothing to do with
JavaScript. The trademark system was never meant to let companies squat on
commonly-used names and rent-seek – it was designed to protect active brands in
commerce. US law makes this distinction explicit.
We urge you to read
our petition
and
open letter
to understand our arguments.
If we don’t win discovery, Oracle locks in ownership of the word “JavaScript.”
This is the decisive moment.
But this case is bigger than JavaScript. It’s about whether trademark law works
as written, or whether billion-dollar corporations can ignore the rule that
trademarks cannot be generic or abandoned. “JavaScript” is obviously both. If
Oracle wins anyway, it undermines the integrity of the whole system.
Let’s make sure the law holds.
Please donate
.
Please share and upvote this.

data.title: Lightweight, highly accurate line and paragraph detection
data.author: colonCapitalDee
data.article_summary: 本文提出了一种基于图卷积网络(GCN)的统一方法来检测文档中的文本行和段落。该方法将任务表述为一个两级聚类问题：第一级将文本检测框聚类为文本行，第二级将文本行聚类为段落。实验表明，该方法在保持高效的同时，在公开数据集和真实图像上的段落检测质量达到了最先进水平。该论文已被DAS 2022会议接受为口头报告论文。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[PDF文档布局分析与文本重构技术的现状与挑战]

不同观点：
• **技术历史与应用**  
  - JKCalhoun提到Apple工程师十年前开发的"tap to zoom"功能，通过识别PDF字符边界框重构段落/表格，但实际应用被简化为点击缩放功能  
  - mcswell指出该领域属于"document structure analysis"，提及十年前处理双语词典OCR时，识别粗体/斜体文本反而是最大难点

• **当前技术局限性**  
  - alsetmusic两周前尝试提取含图片的在线书籍文本失败，现有工具在重构自然文本流方面表现糟糕  
  - VeejayRampay补充指出现有PDF页面分类器（特别是表格识别）可靠性极低

• **潜在应用场景**  
  - throwaway81523认为该技术应整合到浏览器阅读模式  
  - kalev提出能否改进YouTube逐字显示的字幕生成方式

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：看似简单的文档布局分析实际存在巨大技术复杂度（alsetmusic的实践失败 vs "ought to be straightforward"的预期）  
• 文献关联性质疑：mcswell认为论文可能未充分讨论既有文献  
• 讽刺性观察：HocusLocus指出关于PDF分析的论文本身以PDF格式发布  
• 重复提交问题：msephton指出该话题是重复讨论

Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
arXiv:2203.09638
(cs)
[Submitted on 17 Mar 2022]
Title:
Unified Line and Paragraph Detection by Graph Convolutional Networks
Authors:
Shuang Liu
,
Renshen Wang
,
Michalis Raptis
,
Yasuhisa Fujii
View a PDF of the paper titled Unified Line and Paragraph Detection by Graph Convolutional Networks, by Shuang Liu and 3 other authors
View PDF
Abstract:
We formulate the task of detecting lines and paragraphs in a document into a unified two-level clustering problem. Given a set of text detection boxes that roughly correspond to words, a text line is a cluster of boxes and a paragraph is a cluster of lines. These clusters form a two-level tree that represents a major part of the layout of a document. We use a graph convolutional network to predict the relations between text detection boxes and then build both levels of clusters from these predictions. Experimentally, we demonstrate that the unified approach can be highly efficient while still achieving state-of-the-art quality for detecting paragraphs in public benchmarks and real-world images.

Accepted to DAS 2022 as an oral paper

OS-1000-lines-zig
Project Overview
The OS-1000-lines-zig repository is a Zig-based operating system project. The primary purpose of this project is to create a simple, lightweight operating system with a focus on performance and scalability. The key features of this project include:
A monolithic kernel architecture
Support for basic process management and memory management
A simple command-line interface
Getting Started
To get started with the OS-1000-lines-zig project, you will need to have the following prerequisites installed on your system:
Zig compiler (version 0.10.0 or later)
A code editor or IDE of your choice
A terminal or command prompt
To install the project, follow these steps:
Clone the repository using the command
git clone https://github.com/botirk38/OS-1000-lines-zig.git
Navigate to the project directory using the command
cd OS-1000-lines-zig
Build the project using the command
zig build
Usage
To use the OS-1000-lines-zig project, follow these steps:
Run the project using the command
zig run
Interact with the command-line interface to execute commands and view output
Some basic examples of usage include:
Running a simple "Hello World" program
Viewing system information such as memory usage and process list
Architecture Overview
The OS-1000-lines-zig project uses a monolithic kernel architecture, which means that the kernel and user space are combined into a single executable. The kernel is responsible for managing processes, memory, and other system resources.
The project includes several key components, including:
src/kernel.zig
: The kernel implementation, which provides basic process management and memory management functionality.
src/common.zig
: A utility file that provides common functions and macros used throughout the project.
build.zig
: The build script, which is used to compile and link the project.
Configuration
The project uses a simple configuration file to store settings and options. To modify the configuration, edit the
config.zig
file and rebuild the project.
Contributing
Contributions to the project are welcome! To contribute, please fork the repository and submit a pull request with your changes.

LICENSE
file for more information.
Testing and Validation
The project includes automated tests and validation scripts to ensure its correctness and stability. To run the tests, use the command
zig test
.

There are several areas for future development and expansion of the operating system, including:
Adding support for more advanced process management and memory management features
Implementing a more robust command-line interface
Adding support for networking and file systems

data.title: Be careful with Go struct embedding
data.author: mattjhall
data.article_summary: 本文警告Go语言中结构体嵌入(Struct Embedding)功能可能带来的陷阱。文章通过示例说明，当多个嵌入结构体包含相同字段名时，Go会优先访问最外层字段而非报错，这可能导致预期外的行为。作者以实际工作中遇到的类似问题为例，提醒开发者在使用结构体嵌入时要特别小心这种字段名冲突的情况。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Go语言中结构体嵌入（struct embedding）的设计合理性和实际应用中的问题

不同观点：
• **支持嵌入的实用价值**  
  - [lowmagnet] 认为嵌入在特定场景下非常有用，如扩展AWS分页客户端功能  
  - [Olreich] 指出可通过显式路径（如`opts.BarService.URL`）解决字段冲突，并提到嵌入在共享通用字段（如响应对象）时具有优势  

• **反对嵌入的设计缺陷**  
  - [nemo1618] 强烈反对嵌入，认为其几乎总是错误，建议限制使用（如归入`unsafe`特性）  
  - [alpb] 在代码审查中常建议初学者避免嵌入，仅认可在模拟接口部分实现时的有限用途  
  - [tymscar] 质疑编译器未全面处理多层级嵌入冲突（如通过哈希表统一处理），认为特性设计不合理  

• **行为争议与语言设计批评**  
  - [noisy_boy] 和 [Fire-Dragon-DoL] 认为浅层字段优先的行为符合直觉（`abc.com`输出正确）  
  - [preommr] 讽刺Go语言故意设计矛盾特性（如嵌入的复杂性vs缺少`while`循环的"简单性"）  
  - [digianarchist] 将嵌入列为Go语言的"粗糙边缘"之一  

补充讨论：
- **技术细节争议**：  
  - [joahnn_s] 引用语言规范解释字段解析规则（最浅深度优先），[bilbo-b-baggins] 提到IDE会警告此类问题  
  - [okibry] 补充反射标签（如`json`）在嵌入时同样存在冲突问题  
- **替代方案建议**：  
  - [b_e_n_t_o_n] 指出嵌入本质是语法糖，显式声明（如`MyType.MyField`）更清晰

Matt Hall

Be Careful with Go Struct Embedding
Go has a feature called struct embedding that allows you to compose types. It looks something like this:
type
Position
struct
{
X
int
Y
int
}
type
Colour
struct
{
R
byte
G
byte
B
byte
}
type
Rectangle
struct
{
Position
Colour
Width
int
Height
int
}
r
:=
Rectangle
{
/* ... */
}
// This works:
fmt
.
Printf
(
"%d,%d\n"
,
r
.
Position
.
X
,
r
.
Position
.
Y
)
// but so does this:
fmt
.
Printf
(
"%d,%d\n"
,
r
.
X
,
r
.
Y
)
But what do you think this code does?
type
FooService
struct
{
URL
string
}
type
BarConnectionOptions
struct
{
URL
string
}
type
BarService
struct
{
BarConnectionOptions
}
type
Options
struct
{
FooService
BarService
}
opts
:=
Options
{
FooService
:
FooService
{
URL
:
"abc.com"
},
BarService
:
BarService
{
BarConnectionOptions
:
BarConnectionOptions
{
URL
:
"xyz.com"
,
},
},
}
fmt
.
Println
(
opts
.
URL
)
I would expect this to fail to compile as
URL
is ambiguous. It actually prints
abc.com
, presumably as it is the least nested version of that field. This happened at the day job, although it was caught in a test. Be careful when embedding structs!

data.title: My new Git utility `what-changed-twice` needs a new name
data.author: jamesbowman
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是Mark Dominus（陶敏修）的个人博客文章，介绍了自己开发的一个名为`what-changed-twice`（临时命名为Fred）的Git工具。该工具主要用于分析多次修改的文件，帮助用户在多个提交中识别并整理相关的更改。作者还提供了工具的使用示例和输出报告的解释，并邀请读者为工具建议更好的名称。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[工具命名、功能描述及改进建议]

不同观点：
• [GuB-42] 认为现有名称 "what-changed-twice" 已经足够清晰，尽管 "twice" 可能不完全准确（因为可能多次修改），但逻辑上仍然成立。
• [squeaky-clean] 支持现有名称，认为它能准确描述功能，而其他建议（如 "squash-what"）反而更不清晰。
• [handsclean] 建议使用更明确的名称，如 "group-commits-by-file"，认为 "what" 和 "changed" 不够准确，且工具的功能不仅仅是检测变化。
• [quuxplusone] 提议使用 "git squash-report"，认为这样更符合 Git 工具命名习惯，且不会干扰现有命令的补全。
• [zahlman] 建议遵循 Git 工具的命名惯例，如 "git-repeatedly-changed"，以便于记忆和补全。
• [allseeingimei] 提出 "git-delta -n <times>" 的方案，认为可以通过参数灵活指定修改次数。

补充讨论：
• 功能扩展：[gorgoiler] 指出该工具可以进一步扩展为多个子工具，如构建依赖图、自动化提交重组等，但作者的使用场景较为局限。
• 技术细节：[eru] 提醒工具的输出仅适用于文本层面的冲突检测，语义上的冲突（如测试失败）仍需人工检查。
• 输出优化：[nferraz] 建议简化输出格式，省略冗余的缩写 ID，直接显示完整 ID。
• 其他建议：[codewritero] 提到 Jujutsu 的 "absorb" 命令可能提供类似功能；[MontagFTB] 则类比了 "gather" 算法。

My new git utility `what-changed-twice` needs a new name
As I have
explained in the past
, my typical workflow is to go
along commiting stuff that might or might not make sense, then clean it
all up at the end, doing multiple passes with
git-add
and
git-rebase
to get related changes into the same commit, and then to order the
commits in a sensible way. Yesterday I built a new utility that I found
helpful.  I couldn't think of a name for it, so I called it
what-changed-twice
, which is not great but my I am bad at naming
things and my first attempt was
analyze-commits
. I welcome
suggestions. In this article I will call it Fred.
What is Fred for?  I have a couple of uses for it so far.
Often as I work I'll produce a chain of commits that looks like
this:
470947ff minor corrections
d630bf32 continue work on `jq` series
c24b8b24 wip
f4695e97 fix link
a8aa1a5c sp
5f1d7a61 WIP
a337696f Where is the quincunx on the quincunx?
39fe1810 new article: The fivefold symmetry of the quince
0a5a8e2e update broken link
196e7491 sp
bdc781f6 new article: fpuzhpx
40c52f47 merge old and new seasons articles and publish
b59441cd finish updating with Star Wars Droids
537a3545 droids and BJ and the Bear
d142598c Add nicely formatted season tables to this old article
19340470 mention numberphile video
It often happens that I will modify a file on Monday, modify it some
more on Tuesday, correct a spelling error on Wednesday. I might have
made 7 sets of changes to the main file, of which 4 are related, 2
others are related to each other but not to the other 4, and the last
one is unrelated to any of the rest. When a file has changed more than
once, I need to see what changed and then group the changes into related
sets.
The
sp
commits are spelling corrections; if the error was made in the
same unmerged topic branch  I will want to squash the correction into
the original commit so that the error never appears at all.
Some files changed only once, and I don't need to think about those at
this stage.  Later I can go back and split up those commits if it seems
to make the history clearer.
Fred takes the output of
git-log
for the commits you are interested
in:
$ git log --stat -20 main...topic | /tmp/what-changed-twice
It finds which files were modified in which commits, and it prints a
report about any file that was modified in more than one commit:
calendar/seasons.blog  196 40 d1
math/centrifuge.blog  193 33
misc/straight-men.blog  53 b5 bd
prog/jq-2.blog  33 5f d6
193  1934047
196  196e749
33  33a2304
40  40c52f4
53  537a354
5f  5f1d7a6
b5  b59441c
bd  bdc781f
d1  d142598
d6  d630bf3
The report is in two parts.  At the top, the path of each file that
changed more than once in the log, and the (highly-abbreviated) commit
IDs of the commits in which it changed.  For example,
calendar/seasons.blog
changed in commits
196
,
40
, and
d1
.  The
second part of the report explains that
196
is actually an
abbreviation for commit
196e749
.
Now I can look to see what else changed in those three commits:
$ git show --stat 196e749 40c52f4 d142598
then look at the changes to
calendar/seasons.blog
in those three
commits
$ git show 196e74 40c52f4 d142598 -- calendar/seasons.blog
and then decide if there are any changes I might like to squash
together.
Many other files changed on the branch, but I only have to concern
myself with four.
There's bonus information too.  If a commit is
not
mentioned in the
report, then it only changed files that didn't change in any other
commit.  That means
45327059.article_summary: 这篇文章是Mark Dominus（陶敏修）的个人博客文章，介绍了自己开发的一个名为`what-changed-twice`（临时命名为Fred）的Git工具。该工具主要用于分析多次修改的文件，帮助用户在多个提交中识别并整理相关的更改。作者还提供了工具的使用示例和输出报告的解释，并邀请读者为工具建议更好的名称。

主要讨论点：[工具命名、功能描述及改进建议]

不同观点：
• [GuB-42] 认为现有名称 "what-changed-twice" 已经足够清晰，尽管 "twice" 可能不完全准确（因为可能多次修改），但逻辑上仍然成立。
• [squeaky-clean] 支持现有名称，认为它能准确描述功能，而其他建议（如 "squash-what"）反而更不清晰。
• [handsclean] 建议使用更明确的名称，如 "group-commits-by-file"，认为 "what" 和 "changed" 不够准确，且工具的功能不仅仅是检测变化。
• [quuxplusone] 提议使用 "git squash-report"，认为这样更符合 Git 工具命名习惯，且不会干扰现有命令的补全。
• [zahlman] 建议遵循 Git 工具的命名惯例，如 "git-repeatedly-changed"，以便于记忆和补全。
• [allseeingimei] 提出 "git-delta -n <times>" 的方案，认为可以通过参数灵活指定修改次数。

补充讨论：
• 功能扩展：[gorgoiler] 指出该工具可以进一步扩展为多个子工具，如构建依赖图、自动化提交重组等，但作者的使用场景较为局限。
• 技术细节：[eru] 提醒工具的输出仅适用于文本层面的冲突检测，语义上的冲突（如测试失败）仍需人工检查。
• 输出优化：[nferraz] 建议简化输出格式，省略冗余的缩写 ID，直接显示完整 ID。
• 其他建议：[codewritero] 提到 Jujutsu 的 "absorb" 命令可能提供类似功能；[MontagFTB] 则类比了 "gather" 算法。

data.title: Procedural Island Generation (VI)
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary:
本文是程序化岛屿生成系列的最后一篇，总结了这个项目的最终步骤和输出成果。主要内容包括：

1. 地形烘焙：将TerrainBuilder状态转换为可重用资产，保留高程、湿度、生物群系和河流等元数据，并修剪生成过程中使用的保护环。

2. CPU调试渲染器：所有图像都在CPU上渲染，包含一系列光栅化工具，确保在不同平台上输出一致。

3. 交互式查看器：提供参数调整、地形绘制和动画工具等功能，支持实时预览和修改。

4. 导出功能：支持将烘焙数据导出为GLB文件、PNG图像和GIF动画，方便在其他工具中使用。

5. 性能概况：各阶段处理时间较短，如27K站点地图在烘焙阶段约6毫秒，渲染生物群系视图约8毫秒。

这些步骤完成了从数学表示到可视化输出的整个流程，生成了包含丰富元数据的紧凑网格结构。

45326690.article_content:
This is the final installment of our procedural island generation series. After building the mesh foundation (
Part I
), painting elevation hints (
Part II
), adding mountain detail (
Part III
), simulating hydrology (
Part IV
), and colouring the terrain with our biome ramp (
Part V
), it is time to package the result. CartoKit finishes by baking the terrain into a compact mesh, visualising it through an egui viewer, and exporting artefacts for other tools.
The journey from mathematical representation to visual output ends with three components:
Terrain::from_terrain
– a baked mesh carrying elevation, moisture, biome, and river metadata.
The debug renderer & viewer
– CPU rasterisers that turn the data into diagnostic images.
Export helpers
– GLB export, PNG captures, and GIF generation built on the same primitives.
Let’s look at each piece.
Baked Terrain Output
Terrain::from_terrain
(
src/terrain.rs:368
) distils the incremental
TerrainBuilder
state into a reusable asset. The bake step:
Keeps only faces whose centroids lie inside the unit square, trimming the guard ring used during generation.
Copies vertex elevation and moisture into mesh attributes so downstream tools can query them directly.
Tags every face with average elevation, a
TerrainType
(land vs. ocean), and the coarse
BiomeType
classification introduced in Part V.
Marks edges as regular, coastline, or river and stores river-flow magnitudes when a
RiverSystem
is present.
The baked mesh is still a
TopoMesh
, meaning we retain the halfedge connectivity that made the earlier stages convenient. When you call
Terrain::from_terrain(&builder)
, you get a self-contained structure that is ready for export or further processing without touching the heavy generation code again.
CPU Debug Renderer
All of CartoKit’s imagery is rendered on the CPU. The
cartokit::debug
module contains a suite of rasterisers—triangle fill, watertight line drawing, paint-map sampling, rainfall heatmaps—that output directly into
image::RgbaImage
buffers. The viewer’s
DisplayRenderer
(
examples/viewer/display_modes.rs
) wires those helpers together:
Mesh modes (
SeedPoints
,
Delaunay
,
Voronoi
,
Quads
,
FinalTriangulation
) call
draw_topokit_mesh
with optional vertex overlays.
Scalar fields (
TriangleElevation
,
DistanceField
,
Rainfall
,
Humidity
,
RiverFlow
,
Biome
) delegate to
draw_triangles_opt
/
draw_regions_opt
with palette swaps.
Noise visualisations reuse the same pipeline, just swapping in different
TriangleProperty
variants.
Because everything renders to software images, the viewer behaves the same on every platform, and the exported screenshots and GIFs are bit-for-bit identical to what you see on screen.
Interactive Viewer
The
cartokit_viewer
example wraps those images in an egui/eframe interface:
The right-hand parameter panel exposes seeds, Bridson separation, rainfall, and river controls, regenerating the terrain whenever you tweak them.
The “Paint Terrain” mode lets you brush elevation hints onto the 128×128 paint map; the next regeneration integrates those hints into the terrain.
Display modes cover the full pipeline: seed classification, mesh structure, mountain distance fields, rainfall, humidity, river diagnostics, biome colours, and the final shaded map.
Animation tools (
examples/viewer/animation.rs
) let you scrub parameters over time and queue frame exports.
Each frame, the viewer renders the active mode into an
RgbaImage
, uploads it as an egui texture, and then recycles the same image for exports. There is no separate rendering path—what you export is exactly what you preview.
Export Helpers
Three helpers in
examples/viewer/export.rs
turn the baked data into files:
// 1. Bake + GLB export via MeshKit
display
::
export_mesh
(
&
terrain_builder
,
seed
);
// 2. One PNG per display mode
display
::
export_all_images
(
seed
,
&
modes
,
|
mode
|
renderer
.render
(
mode
));
// 3. Thumbnail tiles for quick comparisons
display
::
export_all_images_tile
(
seed
,
&
modes
,
|
mode
|
renderer
.render
(
mode
));
export_mesh
clones the baked
Terrain
, rescales coordinates for GLTF’s Y‑up convention, and calls
meshkit::io::save_mesh
to produce a
.glb
file that loads cleanly in Blender or other viewers.
export_all_images
walks every display mode and drops the rendered PNGs into
exports/images_seed_<seed>/
.
export_all_images_tile
cuts out the top-left 1/8×1/8 tile from each image—handy for diffing or documentation thumbnails.
For animated parameter studies,
examples/viewer/gif_export.rs
converts a list of pre-rendered frames into a looping GIF, with options for downsampling, FPS, and output directory naming.
Performance Snapshot
Generation times were covered in the earlier posts (≈80 ms for the default 27 K-site map on a modern desktop). The finishing steps add little overhead:

CPU render – biome view

GLB export (
meshkit::io::save_mesh
)

PNG capture per display mode

data.title: Zig got a new ELF linker and it's fast
data.author: Retro_Dev
data.article_summary: Zig编程语言项目合并了一个新ELF链接器Elf2的开发提交。新链接器可通过`-fnew-linker`参数启用，在增量编译模式下默认使用。性能测试显示，使用新链接器后增量更新速度提升11倍，仅比跳过代码生成和链接慢4%。该PR还关闭了相关issue #24110，新链接器已通过所有x86_64-linux平台的增量测试。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[Zig语言及其工具链的优势和应用场景]

不同观点：
• [olivia-banks] 认为Zig的垂直集成堆栈（包括自定义链接器和代码生成后端）是其突出特点，能够实现有趣的优化，并且与C相比，编译器交互更加一致。他将其用作语言项目的实验性后端，取得了良好的效果。
• [rstat1] 对Zig语言本身不感兴趣，但认为Zig作为独立的C/C++编译器非常出色，特别是在跨平台编译方面（如linux-arm64），比传统的Linux发行版提供的工具更简单易用。
• [squirrellous] 关注Zig的链接器（elf2）是否可以独立用于C/C++工具链，或者是否仅为Zig定制，认为链接器领域正在经历复兴。
• [chris_armstrong] 提到Zig的链接器是其成为完全自包含的跨平台C工具链的关键部分，尤其是在支持更多平台/格式后。
• [dustbunny] 高度评价Zig，认为其构建系统使其成为下一代最佳语言。

补充讨论：
• [edoceo] 提到Zig修复了调试输出的一个bug，认为这一点比速度更重要。
• [esbranson] 推荐了《Linkers and Loaders》一书，暗示链接器技术的复杂性。

争议焦点：
• Zig的主要优势是语言本身还是其工具链（如编译器和链接器）？
• Zig的链接器是否可以独立用于非Zig项目？

45290636.article_content:
Science
Discovering new solutions to century-old problems in fluid dynamics
Published
18 September 2025
Authors
Yongji Wang, Sam Blackwell
Share
Copy link
×
Our new method could help mathematicians leverage AI techniques to tackle long-standing challenges in mathematics, physics and engineering.
For centuries, mathematicians have developed complex equations to describe the fundamental physics involved in fluid dynamics. These laws govern everything from the swirling vortex of a hurricane to airflow lifting an airplane’s wing.
Experts can carefully craft scenarios that make theory go against practice, leading to situations which could never physically happen. These situations, such as when quantities like velocity or pressure become infinite, are called ‘singularities’ or ‘blow ups’. They help mathematicians identify fundamental limitations in the equations of fluid dynamics, and help improve our understanding of how the physical world functions.
In a
new paper
, we introduce an entirely new family of mathematical blow ups to some of the most complex equations that describe fluid motion. We’re publishing this work in collaboration with mathematicians and geophysicists from institutions including Brown University, New York University and Stanford University
Our approach presents a new way to leverage AI techniques to tackle longstanding challenges in mathematics, physics and engineering that demand unprecedented accuracy and interpretability.
The importance of unstable singularities
Stability is a crucial aspect of singularity formation. A singularity is considered stable if it is robust to small changes. Conversely, an unstable singularity requires extremely precise conditions.
It’s expected that unstable singularities play a major role in foundational questions in fluid dynamics because mathematicians believe no stable singularities exist for the complex boundary-free 3D
Euler
and
Navier-Stokes
equations. Finding any singularity in the Navier-Stokes equations is one of the six famous
Millennium Prize Problems
that are still unsolved.
With our novel AI methods, we presented the first systematic discovery of new families of unstable singularities across three different fluid equations. We also observed a pattern emerging as the solutions become increasingly unstable. The number characterizing the speed of the blow up, lambda (λ), can be plotted against the order of instability, which is the number of unique ways the solution can deviate from the blow up. The pattern was visible in two of the equations studied, the Incompressible Porous Media (IPM) and Boussinesq equations. This suggests the existence of more unstable solutions, whose hypothesized lambda values lie along the same line.
Line chart with our results showing a surprisingly clear pattern in lambda (λ), a key parameter representing the speed of the blow up, as we found increasingly unstable solutions. This pattern was visible in both the Incompressible Porous Media (IPM) and Boussinesq equations.
We discovered these singularities by incorporating machine learning techniques such as second order optimizers for training neural networks. These methods allowed us to refine our accuracy to an unprecedented level. For reference, our largest errors addressed are equivalent to predicting the diameter of the Earth to within a few centimeters.
Here we show an example of the vorticity (Ω) field found for one of the equations studied. This is a measure of how much the fluid is spinning at each point.
Visualization of a three-dimensional representation and the two-dimensional vorticity (Ω) field found for one of the equations studied.
We also show a one-dimensional slice through the same field along an axis for all of the instabilities we discovered, showing the evolution of increasingly unstable singularities.
Line graph showing a one-dimensional slice through the same two-dimensional vorticity (Ω) field shown above, showing the evolution of increasingly unstable singularities.
Novel method navigates a vast landscape of singularities
Our approach is based on the use of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). Unlike conventional neural networks that learn from vast datasets, we trained our models to match equations which model the laws of physics. The network's output is constantly checked against what the physical equations expect, and it learns by minimizing its ‘residual’, the amount by which its solution fails to satisfy the equations.
“
By embedding mathematical insights and achieving extreme precision, we transformed PINNs into a discovery tool that finds elusive singularities.
Yongji Wang, first author of the study and Postdoctoral Researcher at NYU.
Our use of PINNs goes beyond their typical role as general-purpose tools used for solving partial differential equations (
PDEs
). By embedding mathematical insights directly into the training, we were able to capture elusive solutions — such as unstable singularities — that have long-challenged conventiona

data.title: Model Flop Utilization Beyond 6ND
data.author: brrrrrm
data.article_summary:
本文指出，当前AI行业广泛使用的计算效率指标MFU（Model FLOPs Utilization）存在严重估算不准确的问题，而该指标正指导着数十亿美元的计算资源优化。作者认为：

1. 当前主流近似公式（6ND/2ND）过于简化，假设所有操作都是计算密集型的乘法累加，且忽略了许多实际因素。

2. 随着模型发展，公式面临多个挑战：
- 注意力机制的非线性特性
- 混合专家模型(MoE)中活跃参数计算复杂
- 大规模并行训练的协调难度
- 推理场景下连续批处理带来的资源利用波动

3. 虽然对小规模预训练仍适用，但在现代长序列推理、MoE模型等场景下，传统MFU计算已不能准确反映实际计算效率。

作者呼吁行业需要更精确的MFU计算方法，以更好地优化日益增长的AI计算资源消耗。

45289862.article_content:
# MFU is Poorly Approximating Billions of Dollars in Compute
by [@bwasti](https://x.com/bwasti)
---
Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU) is ***the*** efficiency metric these days.
It captures the utilization of GPUs
either during training or inference.
In turn,
it effectively
quantifies the optimization opportunities available
on billions of dollars of compute.
And it's incredibly approximate.
### Billions?
Google tells me we used ~450TWh of electricity across AI datacenters
last year (2024).  At a very cheap 5¢/kWh we're
talking over $20B in electricity alone.
This number isn't getting smaller.
### Naive?
The most common approximation for MFU is extremely rough:
$$
F_{i} = 2\cdot ND \\\\
F_{t} = 3 \cdot F_{i} = 6\cdot ND
$$
Where $F$ is model flops, $i$ is inference, $t$ training.
$N$ is the number of parameters in a model and $D$ is the
length of the input (or maybe output ... "sequence length").
### What's so bad about 6ND?
To derive $6ND$ we assume these three things:
1. every parameter contributes a single multiply-add (2 flops)
2. backward is 2x as expensive as forward (thus, 3x total)
3. everything is [compute bound](https://docs.nersc.gov/tools/performance/roofline/)
Yea, the *main* optimization metric used on billions of dollars of compute
across the industry is typically heavily approximated by these assumptions.
Nuts!
### Issues *[[i.e. pedantic stuff]]*
Ok I lied 6ND is not dead.  For small labs pre-training models,
the 6ND approximation is probably fine.
Why?
In those domains everything *is* compute-bound and FMA dominated by
the FFNs.
That's what the approximation has lasted so long.
![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:1400/0*ok-RS42aL3-_W1vK)
But most modern large-scale training is **inference-bound** (due to test-time scaling, see above).
Beyond that, product serving demand is growing as a rapid click.
For inference 2ND is definitely problematic.  It rarely captures
the true MFU being achieved, since there are *so* many confounding variables.
***Attention is all I bleed***
First, and most trivially, $D$ is linear and attention is not actually linear.
However, if your sequence length is "short" (I'm talking thousands of tokens),
you are usually bounded by the [FFNs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multilayer_perceptron)
within LLMs.  So fuck it, $D \approx D^2$.
When sequences get long (when is that? depends on the model)
we have adjust by the O($N^2$) attention scaling.
Keep in mind, this has to be done within each batch lane, so the true flop
count ends up looking quite complex.
Thanks [Horace](https://x.com/chhillee) for pointing that out!
![](https://pytorch.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/image-27.png)
And what about more modern attention mechanisms?  These often interleave
local attention to save on compute and induce context length generalization.
So we have to be extra careful when the sequence length get long!
***Mo' Experts Mo' Problems***
![](https://i.imgur.com/OVUon7b.png)
Mixture-of-expert models are all the rage and unfortunately that means
the trusty $N$ in our $6ND$ becomes a bit harder to calculate.
Instead of total parameter count, we need active parameter count.
Typically this is just a matter of keeping track of all the details,
which is rather tedious and bug-prone.
For example, OpenAI published gpt-oss's [total active is 5.1B](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-oss/).
The total parameter count is 117B, the number of experts is 128 and 4 are active.
Ah so $4 \cdot \frac{117e9}{128} = 5.1e9$, right?
No, we're not properly handling attention weights and projection layers.
And be careful when shared experts are involved like Deepseek's MoE.
$$
S = \frac{E_{active} \cdot E_{shared}}{E_{routed} \cdot E_{shared}}
$$
In the above
$S$ is a sparsity factor you can use to adjust your $N$ per layer.
***Parallllellism***
Besides always breaking all the time,
training and serving on thousands of GPUs is a fantastically annoying thing to do
because there are *lots* of types of parallelism to manage.
Tensor (err, model) parallelism, pipeline parallelism, data parallelism,
context parallelism, expert parallelism (which is more of a meta-parallelism).
This might seem hard to account for with MFU calculations,
but it isn't.  You just need to divide by the *total* parallelism given
the global size number of FLOPs.
Total parallelism is most easily figured out by counting GPUs rather
than multiplying the numbers above (since lots of paralellism overlaps these days).
***Batching Never Sleeps***
![](https://www.redhat.com/rhdc/managed-files/Continuous%20batching%20for%20requests.png)
In inference no one waits to collect batches
of requests to run them all at once.  That's a training thing.
Everything is done continuously by modern services,
which multiplexes and fields asynchronous requests as fast as it can.
That means, at any given point, your service will probably have some slack
built into it for that $(N+1)^{th}$ request.  Similarly, your service
will constantly be running at different

不同观点：
• **反对使用npx的观点**  
  - npx会在执行时解析依赖，难以预测和执行代码的版本，不利于SBOM（软件物料清单）合规性。

• **依赖管理和锁定版本的重要性**  
  - 建议使用`npm ci`确保锁定文件中的依赖版本一致（HoyaSaxa）。  
  - Rockslide认为锁定每个依赖的精确版本过于极端，推荐使用默认的lockfile机制。  

• **开发环境和CI/CD的安全实践**  
  - condiment提到在无互联网连接的CI环境中手动管理node_modules，虽然繁琐但能提高安全性。  
  - aiahs建议将开发环境放入Docker容器以隔离风险。  

• **全局模块和编辑器扩展的风险**  
  - abejfehr指出全局模块（如`yarn global add`）和编辑器插件（如ESLint、Prettier）可能自动安装最新版本，带来安全隐患。  
  - 缺乏对这些场景的有效解决方案。

• **语言和生态系统层面的改进需求**  
  - dwoldrich认为Node/NPM存在根本性安全问题（如原生二进制混入、未维护包泛滥），呼吁被更安全的替代技术取代。  
  - jimbohn建议在语言层面定义“白名单上下文”以限制模块行为（如禁用系统命令、网络访问）。  

• **工具和社区的补充建议**  
  - ashishbijlani推荐使用Packj工具检测供应链攻击的迹象（如Shell调用、网络通信）。  
  - lrvick主张极端简化依赖：要么彻底审查所有依赖，要么基于标准库自行实现功能。  

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：是否应强制锁定所有依赖版本（Rockslide vs. 其他强调严格锁定的观点）。  
- **未被充分讨论的话题**：本地开发环境隔离（aiahs提出）和编辑器插件的自动依赖更新风险（abejfehr）。  
- **新兴工具**：vet（indigodaddy推荐）和Packj（ashishbijlani）被提及为解决方案的一部分。

45326754.article_summary: 这篇文章总结了防止NPM供应链攻击的安全最佳实践。主要建议包括：开发者应固定依赖版本、包含锁文件、禁用生命周期脚本、设置最小发布年龄、使用权限模型并减少外部依赖；维护者需启用双重认证、创建有限访问令牌、生成来源声明并检查发布文件；其他建议还有使用私有注册表、审计监控工具及支持开源软件。文章涵盖了npm、bun、deno、pnpm和yarn等多种包管理器的安全配置方法。

主要讨论点：[如何防范Node.js和NPM生态系统中的供应链攻击]

不同观点：
• **反对使用npx的观点**  
  - npx会在执行时解析依赖，难以预测和执行代码的版本，不利于SBOM（软件物料清单）合规性。  
  - 2022年的“colors事件”表明npx可能导致依赖问题突然爆发。

• **依赖管理和锁定版本的重要性**  
  - 建议使用`npm ci`确保锁定文件中的依赖版本一致（HoyaSaxa）。  
  - Rockslide认为锁定每个依赖的精确版本过于极端，推荐使用默认的lockfile机制。  

• **开发环境和CI/CD的安全实践**  
  - condiment提到在无互联网连接的CI环境中手动管理node_modules，虽然繁琐但能提高安全性。  
  - aiahs建议将开发环境放入Docker容器以隔离风险。  

• **全局模块和编辑器扩展的风险**  
  - abejfehr指出全局模块（如`yarn global add`）和编辑器插件（如ESLint、Prettier）可能自动安装最新版本，带来安全隐患。  
  - 缺乏对这些场景的有效解决方案。

• **语言和生态系统层面的改进需求**  
  - dwoldrich认为Node/NPM存在根本性安全问题（如原生二进制混入、未维护包泛滥），呼吁被更安全的替代技术取代。  
  - jimbohn建议在语言层面定义“白名单上下文”以限制模块行为（如禁用系统命令、网络访问）。  

• **工具和社区的补充建议**  
  - ashishbijlani推荐使用Packj工具检测供应链攻击的迹象（如Shell调用、网络通信）。  
  - lrvick主张极端简化依赖：要么彻底审查所有依赖，要么基于标准库自行实现功能。

data.title: Why is Venus hell and Earth an Eden?
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了金星为何成为极端恶劣环境而地球却适宜生命的原因。科学家通过对比两颗行星的形成过程和环境演化，发现尽管它们大小相近、构成相似，但金星可能因早期温室效应失控导致水分蒸发，形成高温高压的酸性大气。研究团队利用综合模型模拟地球的未来，试图解答地球是否也会走向类似金星的命运。文章还讨论了太阳亮度随时间增加对行星环境的影响。这项研究旨在揭示行星宜居性的关键因素及地球未来的潜在风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[金星是否是太阳系中最不适合居住的地方，以及地球与金星的环境差异]

不同观点：
• 金星并非完全不适合居住，其大气层在某些方面与地球相似，科学家甚至提出在金星大气层中建立漂浮城市的设想。例如，充氮和氧的大气球可以在30英里高空自然悬浮，那里的重力、环境压力和辐射接近地球，温度为86°F。
• 金星缺乏熔融核心和磁场，这使得其大气层容易受到太阳风的侵蚀，这是其不适合居住的重要原因之一。
• 地球的内部热量调节（如放射性衰变产生的热量）对维持地球的气候和地质活动至关重要，而金星缺乏这种机制，导致其环境极端。

补充讨论：
• 氧气的毒性：早期地球生命曾因氧气积累（大氧化事件）而面临灭绝风险，这表明氧气丰富的环境也可能对生命有害。
• 金星探索的历史：俄罗斯的金星任务被认为是勇敢且令人印象深刻的。
• 地球的特殊性：地球的环境被认为是极其平衡的，这种平衡使得地球成为生命的理想栖息地。
• 长期改造的可能性：在长时间尺度上，金星可能通过大规模的改造（如建造遮阳伞或磁场透镜）变得适合居住。

争议焦点：
• 金星是否真的是太阳系中最不适合居住的地方？部分观点认为金星在某些条件下可能适合人类居住，而另一些观点则强调其极端环境的不适合性。

By

A team of scientists has investigated how Earth’s twin became so inhospitable, and whether the same will happen to our planet.

Why Is Venus Hell and Earth an Eden?
By
Robin George Andrews
September 15, 2025
A team of scientists has investigated how Earth’s twin became so inhospitable, and whether the same will happen to our planet.
Comment
Save Article
Read Later
By
Robin George Andrews
Contributing Writer
September 15, 2025
View PDF/Print Mode
astronomy
climate models
climate science
physics
planetary science
volcanoes
All topics
V
enus is arguably the worst place in the solar system. A cloak of carbon dioxide suffocates the planet, subjecting its surface to skull-crushing pressure. Sulfuric acid rains down through the sickly yellow sky but never reaches the lava-licked ground. Venus is so hot — hot enough to melt lead — that the acid rain evaporates as it’s falling.
The planet’s extreme inhospitality is at the heart of one of the most beguiling mysteries in planetary science. Venus and Earth formed at the same time, from the same geologic building blocks, in pretty much the same part of the solar system. They’re even the same size. So why is Venus a hellscape, and Earth a garden?
A common refrain in the scientific community is that Venus is just several steps ahead — that it represents the end state of all large rocky planets, including Earth. The hypothesis is that these planets eventually lose the ability to sequester planet-warming greenhouse gases in their geologic underbelly. When those gases then accumulate in the atmosphere, the world enters a runaway greenhouse state — like the boiling hot Venusian climate. “Over the years, we’d always heard about Venus being a preview into Earth’s future,” said
Stephen Kane
, a planetary astrophysicist at the University of California, Riverside.
But is that long-held assumption true? In hundreds of millions or billions of years, will Earth’s climate go the way of Venus’, transitioning from a temperate world into a catastrophic hothouse? Kane and his colleagues have been trying to find out. Venus and Earth are often referred to as twins, with Venus being the evil one of the pair. In their Reuniting Twins project, the scientists have developed a digital model of Earth that combines solar physics, volcanology, plate tectonics and climate science. They’ve been pushing their model Earth to its extremes, trying every plausible way to break it and make it into Venus.
As well as exploring what went so wrong on the second rock from the sun, this work speaks to a query closer to home, said
Paul Byrne
, a planetary scientist at Washington University in St. Louis who was not directly involved with the project: “How long is Earth habitable for?”

Venus is 95% as broad as Earth, and 81.5% as massive.
NASA
A Planetary Whodunit
Forecasting Earth’s future requires an understanding of Venus’ past. Long ago, Venus might not have been too different from how Earth is now. Spacecraft surveys and telescope observations have revealed the existence of a rare, heavy form of water in the Venusian atmosphere — a telltale sign that regular water used to be abundant on the planet.
Researchers debate how that water resided there. One possibility is that the water on young Venus formed steam that wafted above the magma sea covering the newborn planet’s surface. That water vapor, a potent greenhouse gas, would have pushed the world into a scorching-hot greenhouse state not long after its birth. Alternatively, Venus’ initial, planetwide magma sea might have cooled and hardened into a crust quickly enough for liquid water — maybe even
an ocean’s worth of water
— to flow across it. If that is true, then what happened to all that water?
In 2020,
Michael Way
, a planetary scientist and climate modeler at NASA’s Goddard Institute for Space Studies in New York, looked at
two possibilities
for how a Venusian ocean could have boiled away.
Why the Sun Is Brightening
O
ur star burns hydrogen in its core, turning it into helium. As helium takes hydrogen’s place, the core becomes denser, which raises the star’s internal pressure. This causes the internal temperature to rise, too. That means that, although there are fewer hydrogen nuclei in the core, they can now zip about fast enough to increase the odds of a (helium-forming) collision. And so, over time, as the internal temperature keeps rising, the sun radiates ever more sunlight. So far, its luminosity has risen 48% since its birth 4.

data.title: Tiny reactors could one day power towns, campuses; community input will be key
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 美国研究人员正在开发小型核反应堆（微反应堆），这种反应堆占地面积小（约一个足球场大小），功率低于20兆瓦，可为城镇、校园等提供清洁能源。微反应堆技术借鉴了早期军用小型反应堆的设计，未来可能在工厂批量生产后运输到使用地点。尽管具有潜在优势，如为偏远社区、数据中心等提供稳定能源，但该技术仍面临成本不确定、公众信任重建等挑战。目前尚未实现商业化生产，需等待订单和工厂建设的进一步推进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[微型核反应堆的可行性和风险]

不同观点：
• [微型核反应堆的安全风险]
  - cool_dude85担心当这些反应堆被废弃或长期缺乏投资和维护时，可能会发生灾难性故障。他举了一个当地水利基础设施因缺乏维护而濒临崩溃的例子，以此类比微型反应堆可能面临的类似风险。
  
• [核能已失去竞争力]
